questions.stem: The planners add a rule: each region must receive a minimum spend. In steps/03, what code is written for it?

options.text: A new loop in build, since every row is written inside build
options.says: Since step 03, build runs the RULES list and no longer changes when a rule is added.

options.text: A change to each rule function, so all of them check the new rule
options.says: Each rule owns only its own rows; the others do not change.

options.text: A new function in rules.py, added to RULES; build stays the same
options.says: Right: a new rule is a new function in the RULES tuple.

options.text: A new class with apply and check methods, registered by its name
options.says: One class per rule was the alternative the design rejected.

origin.section: Each Rule Is a Function That Adds Rows With the Names It Owns

questions.stem: A test checks that a must-do is funded, on data where the must-do also has the highest value and fits the budget. What does the test show?

options.text: That the must row works, since the must-do ends up in the plan
options.says: The must-do would be funded with or without the row, so its presence proves nothing.

options.text: That the rule is missing, since a high-value must-do is skipped
options.says: A high-value project that fits is funded even without the rule.

options.text: That the model is infeasible, since the must-do holds the budget
options.says: Must-dos make a model infeasible only when they ask for more money than there is.

options.text: Nothing about the rule, since the plan funds it without any rule
options.says: Right: the test must use data where the plan without the rule breaks it.

origin.section: A Rule's Test Uses Data Where the Old Plan Breaks That Rule

questions.stem: A child may start only in 2027 and has a one-year lag after its parent, whose window starts in 2027. The plan starts in 2027. What does the child's after row for 2027 say?

options.text: The child cannot start in 2027, since the parent side is an empty sum
options.says: Right: no parent start is as early as 2026, so the row reads started_by(child, 2027) <= 0.

options.text: The child may start in 2027 if its parent starts in 2027 as well
options.says: With a one-year lag the parent must have started by 2026.

options.text: The row is skipped, since a parent side with no terms is not built
options.says: The row is built; its parent side is the empty sum, which fast_sum handles.

options.text: The model is infeasible, since the row has no parent variable in it
options.says: The row only keeps the child out; the rest of the model still has plans.
